screens.body: Copy-pasting the same code in five places is a trap: fix a bug once, and you must fix it five times. A method bundles code under a name so you write it once and call it anywhere. One copy to fix, one copy to improve. That's code reuse — the whole point of methods.

options: Bundles reusable code under a name
check.question: A method…

screens.heading: Methods: name it once, use it forever
screens.keyPoint: Write once, call anywhere — that's code reuse.

screens.body: Defining a method creates it; calling it runs it. The definition says what happens; the call says when. You can call the same method as many times as you want, from anywhere in your program. Define near your other methods, call wherever you need the job done.
screens.heading: Defining and calling
screens.keyPoint: Define the steps; call the name to run them.

screens.body: Methods get more useful with parameters — inputs you hand them when you call. The method declares what it expects (String name); the call supplies the actual value ("Roli"). One method, endless variations: greet("Roli") and greet("Mom") do the same job with different data.
screens.heading: Parameters: inputs
screens.keyPoint: Parameters let one method handle many inputs.

screens.body: Some methods answer back. A return value is the method's output — it hands a value to whoever called it. The method's type says what comes back: int means 'I return a whole number.' The caller usually stores it: int x = doubleIt(7); now x holds 14. return also ends the method immediately.

options: Sends a value back to the caller
check.question: return…

screens.heading: Return values: outputs
screens.keyPoint: return hands a value back to the caller.

screens.body: An array holds many values under one name — a row of labeled boxes. You declare the type with brackets: int[] scores. Each item has an index number starting at 0, so scores[0] is the FIRST item. Arrays have a fixed size: once made, they don't grow.
screens.heading: Arrays: many values, one name
screens.keyPoint: Arrays hold many values; indexes start at 0.

screens.body: Arrays and loops are best friends. A for loop walking i from 0 to scores.length - 1 can touch every item: scores[i]. This pattern — loop through the whole array — is how you total scores, find the biggest value, or print a list. Learn it cold; you'll use it constantly.

check.question: An array of 4 items has valid indexes…

screens.heading: Looping through arrays
screens.keyPoint: Loop 0 to length-1 to visit every item.

screens.body: Scope is where a variable is allowed to live. A variable declared inside a method — including its parameters — exists only inside that method. The outside world can't see it. This is actually protection: methods can't accidentally mess with each other's variables. If you need to share, pass it as a parameter or return it.

check.question: A variable declared inside a method…

screens.heading: Scope: where variables live
screens.keyPoint: Method variables stay inside the method.
